    "Use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) as the test framework, consistent with modern Spring projects",
    "Use Spring Boot Test and Spring Cloud Stream test binders for stream-based sink tests",
    "Use an embedded mock HTTP server (e.g., MockWebServer / WireMock) for the Splunk sink instead of a real Splunk instance to keep CI fast and hermetic",
    "Use an embedded/local Spark context (e.g., spark-submit in local mode or a local SparkSession) for the spark-app batch job acceptance test, avoiding any cluster dependency",
    "Self-contained tests: each acceptance test must start its own application context, send input, and assert on output without depending on pre-existing external services",
    "Use AssertJ for fluent assertions across all test classes",
    "Organize tests under src/test/java/.../acceptance following the same Maven/Gradle module structure as the production code",
    "Add each acceptance test class as an entry point in the CI Maven/Gradle build so that failures fail the build",
    "Each module test class covers: happy path, at least one edge case, and one error/misconfiguration scenario",
    "For the throughput-sampler sink, use time-controlled inputs (e.g., virtual time or controlled bursts) to validate sampling behavior deterministically"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The eight modules already exist with their production source code; the task is to add acceptance test coverage, not to implement the modules",
    "The project uses Maven or Gradle and already has a CI pipeline; only the test invocation wiring needs to be added",
    "An experienced Java/Spring developer performs the work, familiar with Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream, and Apache Spark basics",
    "Workday is 8 hours of focused development effort (no meetings, no interruptions)",
    "No external services (Splunk, Spark cluster, shell binaries beyond standard utilities) are required in CI; mocks and embedded substitutes are acceptable",
    "Existing unit tests exist for some modules but are not considered 'acceptance' tests; they remain untouched",
    "Java 17+ is available in the CI environment, consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 requirements",
    "Acceptance tests must be reliable enough to run on every CI build (target: < 5 minutes total for the new tests)",
    "No new public API or production code changes are needed; only test code and build configuration",
    "Code review and PR submission are not separately estimated (folded into stabilization activity)"
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Test infrastructure review and pattern definition",
      "activity_description": "Examine existing test setup, conventions, and Spring Cloud Stream test binder usage across the project. Define the standard acceptance test layout, naming conventions, and reusable base classes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Shared test utilities and helpers development",
      "activity_description": "Create shared helpers: message generators, embedded HTTP server factory for Splunk, time-control utilities for sampling tests, and test property sources for repeatable configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Null sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests verifying the null sink discards incoming messages without side effects, including a happy path and an error-input path.",
      "most_likely_effort": 0.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Rich-gauge sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests verifying the rich-gauge sink publishes gauge metrics with the expected name, value, and tags, using a captured metric registry or test binder.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Router sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests covering conditional routing logic, including default routes, multiple route conditions, and the fallback/unchanneled behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Shell sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests verifying the shell sink invokes the configured command with message payload, including a simple echo command and an error-exit-code path.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Splunk sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests using an embedded mock HTTP server to verify the Splunk sink posts HEC events with correct payload structure, headers, batching behavior, and HTTP error handling.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Throughput-sampler sink acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests verifying the sampler emits approximately the configured fraction of messages across burst inputs, including deterministic-time scenarios for the 1-in-N and probabilistic modes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.25
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Spark-app batch job acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests that launch the spark-app batch job in local Spark mode against a small test dataset, verifying job completion, output content, and failure handling on bad input.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Timestampfile batch job acceptance tests",
      "activity_description": "Implement acceptance tests that run the timestampfile batch job, verifying that the file is created/updated with the expected timestamp content and that re-runs behave correctly.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "CI build pipeline configuration",
      "activity_description": "Wire the new acceptance test classes into the Maven/Gradle build (Surefire/Failsafe configuration) and the CI job definition, including environment variables and required test resources.",
      "most_likely_effort": 0.75
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Test stabilization and debugging",
      "activity_description": "Run the full suite locally and in CI, fix flakiness, race conditions, and environment-specific issues. Adjust timeouts, ordering, and resource cleanup until the suite is green and stable.",
      "most_likely_effort": 1.5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "Documentation updates",
      "activity_description": "Update module-level and project-level documentation (README, TESTING.adoc) describing the new acceptance test coverage and how to run it locally.",
      "most_likely_effort": 0.5
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 17.5
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use JUnit 5 (Jupiter) as the test framework, consistent with modern Spring projects
Use Spring Boot Test and Spring Cloud Stream test binders for stream-based sink tests
Use an embedded mock HTTP server (e.g., MockWebServer / WireMock) for the Splunk sink instead of a real Splunk instance to keep CI fast and hermetic
Use an embedded/local Spark context (e.g., spark-submit in local mode or a local SparkSession) for the spark-app batch job acceptance test, avoiding any cluster dependency
Self-contained tests: each acceptance test must start its own application context, send input, and assert on output without depending on pre-existing external services
Use AssertJ for fluent assertions across all test classes
Organize tests under src/test/java/.../acceptance following the same Maven/Gradle module structure as the production code
Add each acceptance test class as an entry point in the CI Maven/Gradle build so that failures fail the build
Each module test class covers: happy path, at least one edge case, and one error/misconfiguration scenario
For the throughput-sampler sink, use time-controlled inputs (e.g., virtual time or controlled bursts) to validate sampling behavior deterministically
assumptions: The eight modules already exist with their production source code; the task is to add acceptance test coverage, not to implement the modules
The project uses Maven or Gradle and already has a CI pipeline; only the test invocation wiring needs to be added
An experienced Java/Spring developer performs the work, familiar with Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream, and Apache Spark basics
Workday is 8 hours of focused development effort (no meetings, no interruptions)
No external services (Splunk, Spark cluster, shell binaries beyond standard utilities) are required in CI; mocks and embedded substitutes are acceptable
Existing unit tests exist for some modules but are not considered 'acceptance' tests; they remain untouched
Java 17+ is available in the CI environment, consistent with Spring Framework 6.0 requirements
Acceptance tests must be reliable enough to run on every CI build (target: < 5 minutes total for the new tests)
No new public API or production code changes are needed; only test code and build configuration
Code review and PR submission are not separately estimated (folded into stabilization activity)
